title: Tired Zverev Says He 'Overachieved' by Reaching Shanghai Semifinal
summary:
German tennis star Alexander Zverev reached the semifinals of the Shanghai Masters, but his tournament ended there. Afterward, he said he felt he had "overachieved" because he was so tired.

Zverev, who is ranked world number two, has had a busy schedule. He has had little chance to rest between the US Open, the Laver Cup, the Beijing Masters and Shanghai. He said he came into the event carrying a little bit of injury and fatigue.

"I feel like I've actually, in a way, maybe overachieved this week because of how much tennis I played," Zverev said.

In the semifinal, he played Davidovich Fokina, the tournament's 25th seed. Zverev won the first set. But his opponent hit an excellent backhand passing shot to break Zverev's serve and push the match to a deciding third set. Zverev fell behind 2-0 in that set and could not recover.

Zverev said he had felt "flat" since a tough fourth-round match against Alexander Bublik that went to a third-set tie-break. He did play very well in the quarterfinal, beating Alex de Minaur in straight sets.

"We're all human beings, even the best players in the world," he said.

The loss was a rare disappointment in a brilliant season. Zverev won the first Grand Slam title of his career at the French Open in June, then won a second at the US Open in September. He is also guaranteed to finish the year as world number one, and he will be the first German man to do so.

Davidovich Fokina reached his first ATP Masters 1000 final since 2022. He will face fellow Spaniard Rafael Jodar in the final on Sunday.
why_it_matters: Zverev's comments show that even top athletes get tired and need rest, and that one loss does not erase a great season.
